title: The repository between the network and the store

videos.script: Lesson 12 asked the server every time a screen appeared. On a train, that screen showed nothing. {{train}} The phone had seen the courses that morning. Nothing had kept them. {{repo}} Today the screens stop talking to the network. They ask one object, the repository, and it decides where the answer comes from. {{halves}} It holds two things, known only by protocols. A source, which is lesson 12's client. And a store, which is one JSON file on the device. {{read}} A read never waits. It answers with what the device has, and a refresh replaces it when the server answers. {{write}} A write goes to the device first. It waits in a pending list, and it is sent when the network comes back. {{fake}} Then a fake server, written inside the tests. It goes offline on command. It refuses on command. And it can lose an answer on the way back. {{lost}} That last one is the hard case. The phone cannot know whether the server kept the session. So it sends it again, and the server keeps it once.
